symbols.name: NONE

symbols.signature: const JUSTIFY_SQUEEZE: Squeeze = Squeeze { share: 0.25, word_cap: true, face_bound: false, line_share: 0.0, }

symbols.name: WP_SQUEEZE

symbols.name: SQUEEZE_WORD_SHARE

symbols.signature: const ALL: Allowed = CHANGES | HIGHLIGHT | COMMENT | FIELD | MARK

symbols.name: inside
symbols.signature: fn inside(kind: Allowed, allowed: Allowed) -> Allowed
symbols.doc: What the body of a span of `kind`, itself opened where `allowed`, may open.

symbols.name: Cover
symbols.doc: A nested span's cover of one delimiter position: the innermost span covering it, the earliest start and the latest end of every span covering it.

symbols.name: Run
symbols.doc: A delimiter's run of consecutive covered positions: the first index after it, its earliest covering start, its latest covering end.

symbols.name: count_closer_steps
symbols.doc: Count `steps` closer-search steps.

symbols.name: Closers
symbols.doc: Where every unescaped closer and separator sits in the source, found once so that an opener without its closer does not scan the rest of the text, and the parts Markdown reads literally.

symbols.name: slot
symbols.doc: The delimiter list slot `pattern` occupies.

symbols.name: in_spans
symbols.signature: fn in_spans(spans: &[(usize, usize)], at: usize) -> bool
symbols.doc: Whether `at` is inside one of `spans`, which must be disjoint and sorted.

symbols.name: paired
symbols.signature: fn paired( openers: &[usize], close: &str, inner: &[(usize, usize)], positions: &[Vec<usize>; 6], ) -> Vec<(usize, usize)>
symbols.doc: The spans `open` opens: each opener, skipping any inside an earlier pair or a span of `inner`, with the first `close` after its opener text that `inner` does not hold, so a `{==` whose first `==}` sits in a comment closes past it, as the recursive reader closes it.

symbols.name: keeping_fences
symbols.doc: The reader's fence escapes kept as written, for Markdown a resolve writes back: its code fences still name the same document.

symbols.name: find
symbols.signature: fn find(&self, pattern: &str, from: usize, until: usize) -> Option<usize>
symbols.doc: The first `pattern` that lies whole in `from..until`.

symbols.name: find_outside_nested
symbols.signature: fn find_outside_nested(&self, pattern: &str, from: usize, until: usize) -> Option<usize>
symbols.doc: The first `pattern` that lies whole in `from..until` outside every complete nested span, or inside one whose opener is before `from` or whose closer is past `until`: a comment or highlight is opaque only while it is whole inside the range, so a `~>` or `++}` in its text cannot split or shorten the span around it, and...

symbols.name: paragraph_end
symbols.signature: fn paragraph_end(&self, from: usize, until: usize) -> usize
symbols.doc: Where the paragraph `from` lies in ends: at its blank line, or at `until` if that comes first.

symbols.name: Literal
symbols.doc: The parts of a Markdown source that Markdown reads literally: code spans, link destinations and autolinks (`verbatim`), where nothing opens, and fenced code blocks and the YAML front matter (`fences`), where CriticMarkup still marks tracked changes (the reader prints them there) but `==` and `{CODE}` open nothing: a h...

symbols.name: verbatim_end
symbols.doc: Where the code span, link destination or autolink that `at` lies in ends, if it lies in one.

symbols.name: in_fence
symbols.doc: Whether `at` lies in a fenced code block.

symbols.name: in_code_fence
symbols.doc: Whether `at` lies in a fenced code block, not the front matter: the reader escapes a code block's text for the writer to unwind here.

symbols.name: indented_code
symbols.doc: The byte ranges of CommonMark's indented code blocks: a line indented four or more spaces that nothing contains is one, and pulldown-cmark finds it, a list item's own indent included.

symbols.name: code_span_end
symbols.doc: The end of the code span a backtick run at `at` opens: after the next run of as many backticks, in the same paragraph.

symbols.name: definition_destination
symbols.doc: Where the destination (and title) of a link reference definition (`[label]: destination "title"`) starts in `line`, if the line is one.

symbols.name: destination_ends
symbols.doc: Where each link destination (and title) closes, by where it starts, after `](`: its closing `)`, parentheses balanced, on one line.

symbols.name: comment_end
symbols.doc: The end of the HTML comment that starts at `at` (`<!-- … -->`), if it closes.

symbols.name: autolink_end
symbols.doc: The end of an autolink (`<https://a.example>`) at `at`: a scheme, `:`, then no space or `<` up to `>`.

symbols.name: Check
symbols.doc: What a whole-`encode` pass found amiss, for a caller that warns: positions, line numbers resolved at the end so the scan stays cheap.

symbols.name: encode_spans_checked
symbols.signature: fn encode_spans_checked(source: &str, allowed: Allowed, labels: bool, check: &mut Check) -> String
symbols.doc: [`encode`], opening only the spans `allowed` names, moving footnote labels out of spans only when `labels`, and noting malformed delimiters in `check`.

symbols.name: encode_spans
symbols.signature: fn encode_spans(source: &str, allowed: Allowed, labels: bool) -> String
symbols.doc: [`encode`], opening only the spans `allowed` names, and moving footnote labels out of spans only when `labels`.

symbols.name: encode_spans_kept
symbols.doc: [`encode_spans`] with the reader's fence escapes kept as written: the resolved Markdown still names the document its code blocks hold.

symbols.name: encode_range
symbols.signature: fn encode_range( source: &str, closers: &Closers<'_>, range: std::ops::Range<usize>, allowed: Allowed, labels: bool, check: &mut Check, out: &mut String, )
symbols.doc: [`encode_spans`] for the part of `source` in `range`.

symbols.name: encode_comment
symbols.signature: fn encode_comment( source: &str, closers: &Closers<'_>, body: std::ops::Range<usize>, out: &mut String, )
symbols.doc: A comment's body: text, with every run of blank or whitespace-only lines as one [`Token::CommentBreak`] stand-in so the comment's paragraphs survive the Markdown parser without splitting the paragraph the comment is anchored on.

symbols.name: fence_escape_at
symbols.signature: fn fence_escape_at(source: &str, at: usize) -> Option<(String, usize)>
symbols.doc: The reader's fence escape (`from_docx::critic::escape_code`) at `at`, if one sits there: the document text it names, and how many bytes it takes.

symbols.name: OPENER
symbols.doc: What can follow the backslash run an opener holds (`{` + run).

symbols.name: CLOSER
symbols.doc: What can hold the run a closer escapes (`++` + run + `}`).

symbols.name: FIELD_END
symbols.doc: What closes a body field.

symbols.name: FIELD_NAMES
symbols.doc: The field names ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5 lists.

symbols.name: is_field_code
symbols.doc: Whether `code` is a field code jubarte prints as `{CODE}`: one line, braces only inside a quoted argument (`QUOTE "a}b"`), quotes closed, and a field name from [`FIELD_NAMES`] (in any case) first.

symbols.name: LONGEST_FIELD_CODE
symbols.doc: The longest field code read, in characters: no field code comes near it, and it keeps a paragraph of `{` from being scanned once per brace.

symbols.name: field_code_close
symbols.signature: pub(crate) fn field_code_close(chars: impl Iterator<Item = (usize, char)>) -> Option<usize>
symbols.doc: Where the `}` that closes a field code sits, given the characters after its `{` with their positions: a brace inside a quoted argument (`"a}b"`, `\"` quoting a quote) belongs to the code.

symbols.name: field_code
symbols.signature: fn field_code(source: &str, at: usize, until: usize) -> Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>
symbols.doc: The code of a body field opened at `at` (`{` then a field code, up to the next `}` on the line), if `at` opens one.

symbols.name: field_at
symbols.signature: fn field_at( source: &str, closers: &Closers<'_>, at: usize, until: usize, ) -> Option<(std::ops::Range<usize>, usize)>
symbols.doc: A body field opened at `at`: its code, and where the `{/}` that closes it sits (before `until`), past any field nested in its result: in the same paragraph, or a later one when its `{CODE}` begins a line (see [`field_ends`]).

symbols.name: field_ends
symbols.doc: The `{/}` that closes each body field, by the field's `{`, found in one pass with a stack of open fields: a nested field's `{/}` closes it first, and code spans, link destinations and autolinks are passed over.

symbols.name: opens_paragraph
symbols.doc: Whether the `{` at `at` begins its paragraph's text: only a heading, list or quote marker (`## `, `- `, `1.

symbols.name: mark_close
symbols.signature: fn mark_close(source: &str, closers: &Closers<'_>, at: usize, until: usize) -> Option<usize>
symbols.doc: Where the `==` that closes a highlight opened at `at` sits, if `at` opens one: `==` touching text on its inner side and not part of `{==`, `==}` or a longer run of `=`, closed by such an `==` in the same paragraph (before `until` and any blank line).

symbols.name: mark_closes
symbols.signature: fn mark_closes(source: &str, literal: &Literal, close: usize) -> bool
symbols.doc: Whether the `==` at `close` can close a highlight: touching text on its inner side, not part of `==}` or a longer run of `=`, and read as Markdown.

symbols.name: footnote_label
symbols.doc: The footnote label that starts `text` with the spaces after it (`[^note]: `), as CommonMark footnote definitions are written.

symbols.name: encode_spans_only
symbols.doc: [`encode`] without moving footnote labels: the spans as written, for reading the markup rather than the Markdown.

symbols.name: verbatim_ranges
symbols.doc: The ranges of `source` the Markdown diff escaper must leave alone: the reader's own verbatim (code spans across single line breaks, link destinations, autolinks) plus every complete HTML comment — a backslash inside one changes the comment's text, and the delimiter the escaper would escape drops with the comment anywa...

symbols.name: decode
symbols.doc: The source of text that holds no stand-ins, as it was.

symbols.name: restore
symbols.doc: The source of encoded text as it was written, delimiters and all.

symbols.name: delimiter
symbols.doc: The CriticMarkup a token stands in for.

symbols.name: Piece
symbols.doc: Text or a delimiter, in source order.

symbols.name: Pieces
symbols.doc: Splits parsed text into [`Piece`]s.

symbols.name: feed
symbols.signature: pub(crate) fn feed(&mut self, text: &str, mut emit: impl FnMut(Piece<'_>))
symbols.doc: Calls `emit` with the pieces of `text`.

symbols.name: resolve
symbols.signature: pub(crate) fn resolve(markdown: &str, accept: bool) -> String
symbols.doc: The Markdown with its CriticMarkup resolved: insertions kept and deletions dropped (`accept`), or the other way round; highlights keep their text and comments go.

symbols.name: names_outer
symbols.doc: Whether `note` names, after ` on `, a change the one it follows sits inside (either view's grammar): resolving that change removes its text either way, for rejecting the outer removes what it holds and accepting the inner removes the text.

symbols.name: accept_clauses
symbols.doc: Accepted document clauses omit a wholly deleted paragraph's line break.

symbols.name: resolve_with_policy
symbols.signature: fn resolve_with_policy(markdown: &str, accept: bool, remove_deleted_lines: bool) -> String

symbols.name: encode_counted
symbols.doc: [`encode`] with the closer-search steps it took: the builders in [`Closers::new`] walk the source once each and every lookup is a step, so a linear encode stays within a small constant times the input, while a search that rescans the rest of the text per opener counts that text and crosses any such bound.

symbols.name: a_complete_comment_inside_a_change_is_opaque_to_its_boundaries
symbols.doc: Every payload that, inside a comment, would shorten the enclosing span or steal its separator, with every change kind and every substitution half.

symbols.name: incomplete_comments_and_escaped_comment_openers_do_not_break_changes
symbols.doc: Incomplete comments and comment boundaries that fall outside the enclosing span must not hide its closer or separator.

symbols.name: many_failed_openers_with_comments_stay_linear
symbols.doc: Many failed change openers before many complete comments must not rescann every comment: the lookup stays linear in the input size.

symbols.name: highlight_openers_before_comment_held_closers_stay_linear
symbols.doc: Many highlight openers before many comments holding their kind's closer must not re-skip every comment from each opener: the pairing pass that finds complete spans stays linear too.

symbols.name: every_comment_hides_its_own_delimiters
symbols.doc: A comment after another comment is still opaque: an earlier comment must not hide the later one's delimiters from the boundary lookup.

symbols.name: a_complete_highlight_inside_a_change_is_opaque_to_its_boundaries
symbols.doc: A complete nested highlight is opaque like a comment: a `~>` or a closer inside it does not split or shorten the change around it, and a `==}` inside its own nested comment does not close it.

symbols.name: a_blank_line_inside_a_comment_is_a_comment_paragraph_break
symbols.doc: A blank line inside `{>>…<<}` becomes a comment paragraph break, not a paragraph break in the text the comment is anchored on.

symbols.name: malformed_critic_markup_is_text_with_a_warning
symbols.doc: Malformed CriticMarkup is text, and says so: an opener without its closer or separator, and a closer nothing opened.

symbols.name: character_references_naming_stand_ins_stay_literal
symbols.doc: A numeric character reference that names a stand-in character or the escape is literal text: the Markdown parser decodes references only after CriticMarkup was read, so the decoded character must not arrive as an unescaped delimiter.

symbols.name: a_closer_inside_a_complete_highlight_is_the_highlight_s_text
symbols.doc: A closer inside a complete highlight is the highlight's text, as a closer inside a comment is the comment's: neither warns as a stray.

symbols.name: WORD_DIFF_SIMILARITY
symbols.doc: Lines that share less than this share of their words are replaced whole rather than word by word.

symbols.name: RARE_LINE_SHARE
symbols.doc: A word shared by more old lines than this does not suggest a pairing; candidates come from the rarer words a line has.

symbols.name: MAX_CANDIDATES
symbols.doc: At most this many candidate old lines are scored against one new line.

symbols.name: REFLOW_MAX_BYTES
symbols.doc: A reflow whose two sides hold more than this many bytes is left to the line pairing: Myers on the tokens is O((n+m)·d), and a rewrap this large can have a distance to match.

symbols.name: diff_markdown
symbols.doc: The two text snapshots, `old` and `new`, as one Markdown document whose CriticMarkup holds the changes: accepting them all gives `new`, rejecting them all gives `old`.

symbols.name: opaque_units
symbols.doc: The physical lines of `text`, except that a code span, equation, image, autolink or HTML comment that spans a line break keeps its lines in one unit: [`atoms`] then reads the whole construct, not a line of it.

symbols.name: marker_len
symbols.doc: The length of a line's block markers: indentation, `>` quote markers, a list marker with its task box, or a heading's `#`s.

symbols.name: continues
symbols.doc: Whether a line continues the paragraph of a non-blank line before it: it has text and no block marker, and is not a table row or code fence.

symbols.name: open_paragraph
symbols.doc: Whether text may continue after a line: not blank, not a heading, a table row or a code fence.

symbols.name: table_row
symbols.doc: A table row: the line starts with a pipe.

symbols.name: table_row_change
symbols.signature: pub(super) fn table_row_change(line: &str, open: &str, close: &str) -> String
symbols.doc: A table row added or removed whole: each cell's text is one change, so the row keeps its cells (a table drops text outside them).

symbols.name: escape
symbols.doc: CriticMarkup delimiters in text, escaped so they stay text.

symbols.name: DELIMITERS
symbols.doc: Openers and the separator take the backslash before their first character; closers take it before `}`, which is how the marks are written today (`\{++`, `++\}`, `~\>`).

symbols.name: escape_points
symbols.doc: Byte positions where a backslash must be inserted.

symbols.name: escaped_at
symbols.doc: Whether `at` follows an odd number of backslashes.

symbols.name: Output
symbols.doc: The marked-up document being written, line by line.

symbols.name: append
symbols.doc: Appends to the last line without a line break.

symbols.name: finish
symbols.signature: fn finish(mut self, old_trailing: bool, new_trailing: bool) -> String

symbols.name: add_trailing
symbols.doc: The final line break changed sides.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc: One line of a changed hunk: paired, or only in one version.

symbols.name: reflow
symbols.doc: A hard-wrapped paragraph whose lines all moved, as one word diff.

symbols.name: reflow_body
symbols.doc: Word diff of a reflowed paragraph.

symbols.name: weight
symbols.doc: A word is worth more than the space or line break it moved across.

symbols.name: pair
symbols.signature: fn pair<'a>(olds: &[&'a str], news: &[&'a str]) -> Vec<Entry<'a>>
symbols.doc: Aligns the lines of a hunk by content: the similar lines with the same marker shapes pair up, in order; the rest are marked block by block.

symbols.name: pair_by_similarity
symbols.doc: The similar-line pairs of a hunk, in order.

symbols.name: dice
symbols.doc: Dice coefficient of two sorted id (or word) multisets: twice the size of their intersection, counting repeats, over the sizes summed.

symbols.name: weighted_pairs
symbols.signature: fn weighted_pairs(pairs: &[(usize, usize, f64)], new_len: usize) -> Vec<(usize, usize)>
symbols.doc: The chain of `pairs` (old index, new index, score) with the greatest score sum whose indices strictly increase.

symbols.name: intern
symbols.signature: fn intern<'a>(ids: &mut std::collections::HashMap<&'a str, u32>, word: &'a str) -> u32

symbols.name: body_words
symbols.doc: Words of a line after its block marker.

symbols.name: similarity
symbols.doc: The share of words two lines have in common (0 to 1): twice the longest common subsequence of their words over the sizes summed.

symbols.name: paired
symbols.doc: A line in both versions: its markers, then its text word by word.

symbols.name: change
symbols.doc: A replacement, deletion or insertion of `old` by `new`.

symbols.name: words_diff
symbols.doc: `old` against `new` word by word.

symbols.name: OpenSpan
symbols.doc: A formatting span [`atoms`] is reading: where it started, the range of its text so far, and whether a change anywhere in it covers all of it (an image or an autolink, whose text is as verbatim as its syntax).

symbols.name: Atom
symbols.doc: A span that is read whole: a change that touches its `triggers` covers all of `range`.

symbols.name: atoms
symbols.doc: Numbers (`$5,000,000`, `04/20/26`, `3.5%`), the delimiters of emphasis and strikethrough, link syntax (all but its text), and a whole code span, image or equation.

symbols.name: scan_atoms
symbols.signature: fn scan_atoms(text: &str, offset: usize, math: bool) -> Vec<Atom>
symbols.doc: The parser's spans of `text`, a slice of a line at `offset`, with equations read (`math`) or not.

symbols.name: is_atom_end
symbols.doc: Whether `end` closes a span [`atoms`] reads whole.

symbols.name: extend
symbols.doc: Widens the innermost open span's text to cover `range`.

symbols.name: opens_amount
symbols.doc: Whether `at` is the `$` of a currency amount, with a digit right after it: [`numbers`] reads the sign as part of the amount, so this `$` opens no equation — even where the parser pairs it with a later `$` as math (`$250,000 … exceeds **$5,000,000**`).

symbols.name: numbers
symbols.doc: Runs of digits joined by `,` `.` `/` `:` `-` between digits, with a currency sign before and a `%` after.

symbols.name: touches
symbols.signature: fn touches(range: (usize, usize), span: (usize, usize)) -> bool
symbols.doc: Whether a change over `range` (empty: a point) touches `span`.

symbols.name: widen
symbols.signature: fn widen( mut segments: Vec<(bool, String, String)>, old: &str, new: &str, ) -> Vec<(bool, String, String)>
symbols.doc: Changes that touch a number, a formatting delimiter or a link's syntax, widened to all of it (in both versions), so `$5,000,000` is replaced whole and `*Buyer*` becoming `Buyer` reads as one change.

symbols.name: take
symbols.signature: fn take( segments: &mut Vec<(bool, String, String)>, at: usize, length: usize, into_next: bool, ) -> bool
symbols.doc: Moves `length` bytes (or all) of the segment at `at` into the change next to it: its end into the change after it (`into_next`), or its start into the change before it.

symbols.name: group
symbols.signature: fn group(out: &mut Output, side: Side, lines: &[&str])
symbols.doc: Lines only in one version.

symbols.name: wrap_words
symbols.doc: Words of `text` wrapped to `width` columns, the way a hard wrap joins lines back with a space.

symbols.name: INDEX
symbols.doc: Attribute stamped on every numbered `w:p`: its `pN` index.

symbols.name: TABLE
symbols.doc: Attribute stamped on every top-level `w:tbl`: its `t{N}` number.

symbols.name: REVS
symbols.doc: Attribute stamped on a `w:p` that holds revisions: `kind:tag` entries separated by spaces (`ins:0@AC sub:1+2@AC fmt:3@JD mark-ins:4@AC`), recorded before resolution.

symbols.name: Handles

symbols.name: of
symbols.signature: pub(crate) fn of(&self, author: Option<&str>) -> Option<&str>

symbols.name: unique_date
symbols.doc: The one timestamp all of the author's marks and comments share.

symbols.name: date_range
symbols.doc: `first..last` days of an author with several timestamps.

symbols.name: needs_date
symbols.signature: pub(crate) fn needs_date(&self, author: Option<&str>) -> bool

symbols.name: RevTag
symbols.doc: One logical revision as the id line and the header count it.

symbols.name: hollow
symbols.doc: A change mark that holds no text (`<w:ins/>`, or runs of formatting only): the view shows nothing for it, so it neither joins nor splits.

symbols.name: silent_run
symbols.doc: A run the text prints nothing for: vanished, or holding only empty text and page breaks (the page break is the paragraph's id line).

symbols.name: hidden_run

symbols.name: half_ranges
symbols.doc: Whether `mark` holds the start of a shown comment range that ends past it, and the end of one that starts before it.

symbols.name: walk
symbols.signature: fn walk(e: &Element, handles: &Handles, starts: &mut Vec<String>, ends: &mut Vec<String>)

symbols.name: tag_of
symbols.doc: `12@AC`: the element's `w:id` and its author's handle (`??` for an author the legend does not know: a malformed file, or Word's `w:tblGridChange`, which has no author).

symbols.name: plain_tag_of
symbols.doc: `12@Ana%20Lima%20(2026-…)` for the plain view: the element's `w:id` and its `Author (date)` note in place of a handle, spelled ([`tag_id`], spaces too) so that tags split on none of it.

symbols.name: tag_id
symbols.doc: A `w:id` as an internal tag holds it: the characters tags join and split on (`+`, `|`, `@`, `#`, `?`) and `%` itself spelled `%XX`, so a malformed id such as `1+2` stays one id.

symbols.name: untag_id
symbols.doc: The `w:id` one piece of an internal tag spells ([`tag_id`]).

symbols.name: split_tag
symbols.doc: One internal tag's parts: `header1#1+2@AC` → (`Some("header1")`, `1+2`, `AC`).

symbols.name: handle_of
symbols.doc: The handle of a one-author tag (`1+2@AC` → `AC`); `None` for several.

symbols.name: join_tags
symbols.doc: Joins the tags of one logical change: `1@AC` + `2@AC` is `1+2@AC`, `1@AC` + `2@JD` is `1@AC|2@JD`, `1+2@AC` + `3@AC` is `1+2+3@AC`.

symbols.name: format_tag
symbols.doc: `0@AC` → `r0 @AC`; `1+2@AC` → `r1+2 @AC`; `header1#2@JD` → `header1.r2 @JD`; `1@AC|2@JD` → `r1 @AC; r2 @JD`.

symbols.name: format_plain_tag
symbols.doc: A plain-view tag ([`plain_tag_of`]) as its note prints it: the ids, then the `Author (date)` note when there is one (`r1+2 Ana Lima (2026-09-29T14:05:00Z)`, `r7`).

symbols.name: format_tag_by

symbols.name: format_tags
symbols.doc: A list of tags for an id line: `r0 @AC; r1+2 @AC`.

symbols.name: revision_tags
symbols.doc: The revisions among a paragraph's direct children, in order, as the renderer shows them: neighbouring marks of one kind by one author join (`7+8@AC`), then an insertion directly followed by a deletion pairs as a substitution, greedily left to right.

symbols.name: flatten

symbols.name: mark_tags

symbols.doc: Tags of the formatting changes recorded in a paragraph (its runs' and its own properties, its list number), a text box Word stores twice read once.

symbols.name: split_tag
symbols.doc: A start or end tag: from its `<` to the first `>` outside quoted attribute values (a `>` inside a value is legal XML).

symbols.doc: Copy `tag` to `out`, rewriting only the values of the attributes that carry URIs of `site`.

symbols.name: attr_name
symbols.doc: The attribute name ending `before` — the token after the last whitespace, `=` stripped: `… <w:p xmlns:w=` → `xmlns:w`.

symbols.name: replace_all
symbols.doc: The old whole-string substitution, now scoped to one attribute value.

symbols.name: STRICT_MAIN
symbols.doc: The Strict wordprocessingml main namespace — the URI that makes a main part Strict rather than Transitional.

symbols.name: main_part_is_strict
symbols.doc: Whether the package's main document part (`word/document.xml`) is ISO Strict — decided by the namespace its root element declares, the same fact Word reads the dialect from.

symbols.name: root_open
symbols.doc: Where `head` opens its root element: the first `<` an element name follows (a comment, PI or DOCTYPE `<!`/`<?` opens none).

symbols.name: strict_to_transitional_docx
symbols.doc: Normalize an ISO/IEC 29500 **Strict** `.docx` to **Transitional**.

symbols.doc: [`strict_to_transitional_docx`] with an explicit inflation budget.

symbols.name: text_quoting_a_strict_uri_keeps_it
symbols.doc: A Strict document whose *text* quotes a Strict URI: the namespace declaration is rewritten, the `w:t` keeps the bytes the file's own text carries (#531 review defect 2 — a whole-part `str::replace` rewrote the document's prose as well).

symbols.name: relationship_targets_keep_their_strict_uri
symbols.doc: A Strict `.rels` whose hyperlink `Target` is itself a Strict URI: the relationship `Type` is translated, the target the author linked to stays verbatim.

symbols.name: transitional_package_quoting_a_strict_uri_stays_untouched
symbols.doc: A Transitional package whose text merely mentions a Strict URI is handed back byte-for-byte: the marker in prose no longer counts as a Strict package (#531 review defect 2).

symbols.name: strict_package_keeps_field_text_quoting_a_strict_uri
symbols.doc: A Strict package whose `w:instrText` quotes a Strict URI keeps the instruction's bytes while its namespaces are translated end to end.

symbols.name: translates_strict_document_xml_namespaces
symbols.doc: A Strict `document.xml` snippet: the `w`, `r`, and `m` namespaces flip to their Transitional URIs, and no `purl.oclc.org` survives.

symbols.name: graphic_data_uri_attributes_are_translated
symbols.doc: A Strict `a:graphicData/@uri` — an attribute whose whole value is a namespace URI, not a declaration — is translated with the namespaces, while `mc:Ignorable`, which names prefixes rather than URIs, stays as the file spells it (#561 review defect 1).

symbols.name: translates_strict_rels_including_irregular
symbols.doc: A Strict `.rels` snippet: the IRREGULAR `extendedProperties` rel becomes `extended-properties` (longest-key-first beats the `customProperty`/ `extendedProperty` prefixes), and a regular `styles` rel becomes the Transitional styles rel.

symbols.name: oversized_part_is_left_untouched_under_a_small_budget
symbols.doc: A Strict package whose media part inflates past the part budget is handed back untouched instead of being inflated without bound; the same package passes under the comparer's default budget.

symbols.name: a_long_preamble_does_not_hide_a_strict_root
symbols.doc: A preamble longer than the old 64 KiB window no longer hides the Strict root: the dialect is read from the root's own opening tag, wherever in the part it lies (#561 review defect 2).

symbols.name: transitional_package_returned_byte_identical
symbols.doc: A Transitional package is returned byte-for-byte unchanged (zero-churn).

symbols.name: strict_package_is_rewritten_to_transitional
symbols.doc: A Strict package is actually rewritten (the zero-churn fast path does NOT fire): every text part ends up Transitional.

symbols.doc: Raw 20-byte SHA-1 digest of `bytes`.

symbols.name: hex_encode_20
symbols.doc: Lowercase-hex-encode 20 digest bytes into a fixed 40-byte ASCII buffer (no heap allocation).

symbols.name: hex_decode_20
symbols.doc: Decode exactly 40 hex characters into the 20-byte digest they encode; `None` for any other length or any non-hex character.

symbols.name: sha1_hex_of_digest_hexes
symbols.signature: pub fn sha1_hex_of_digest_hexes<'a, I>(digests: I) -> String where I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a [u8; 20]>,
symbols.doc: SHA-1 of the concatenation of the 40-char lowercase hex encodings of each digest.

symbols.name: sha1_hex_bytes
symbols.doc: Lowercase-hex SHA-1 of `bytes`.

symbols.name: sha1_hex_parts
symbols.signature: pub fn sha1_hex_parts<'a, I>(parts: I) -> String where I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>,
symbols.doc: SHA-1 of the concatenation of `parts`, without allocating the concatenated string.

symbols.name: fnv1a_64
symbols.doc: 64-bit FNV-1a of the string's bytes (offset basis `0xcbf29ce484222325`, prime `0x100000001b3`).

symbols.name: fnv1a_128
symbols.doc: 128-bit FNV-1a of the string's bytes (offset basis `0x6c62272e07bb014262b821756295c58d`, prime `0x1000000000000000000013b`).

symbols.name: sha1_fingerprint
symbols.doc: Former name of [`fnv1a_64`].

symbols.name: sha1_fingerprint128
symbols.doc: Former name of [`fnv1a_128`].

symbols.name: is_continuation
symbols.doc: A combining mark (Unicode category Mn, Mc or Me), an emoji skin tone modifier (U+1F3FB to U+1F3FF, a symbol that behaves like a mark) or the zero width joiner: it continues the token of the character before it.

symbols.name: is_symbol
symbols.doc: A symbol (an emoji, `+`, `$`): a base that marks and joiners attach to.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc: What the token being built is made of.

symbols.name: word_tokens
symbols.doc: Split `text` into a `Vec<&str>` of tokens and return them.

symbols.name: composed_and_decomposed_text_tokenize_alike
symbols.doc: Same text, composed and decomposed: the same number of tokens.

symbols.name: a_mark_without_a_base_is_a_token_of_its_own
symbols.doc: A mark with no letter or digit before it (it follows whitespace, punctuation or the start of the text) never joins that punctuation or whitespace: a run of such marks is a token of its own, and the next word starts a new token.

symbols.name: Finding
symbols.doc: One thing wrong with a package, from any rule set: Word validity (`word`), tracked-edit discipline (`edits`), or the [`crate::audit`] sets (`a11y`, `style`, `structure`).

symbols.name: RULE_SETS
symbols.doc: Every rule set `validate` runs, `word` (the default) first.

symbols.name: new
symbols.signature: pub fn new( code: &str, part: &str, location: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>, ) -> Self
symbols.doc: A `word` finding with `word_fatal` and `repairable` taken from the code's table ([`traits`]) and the severity from `word_fatal`.

symbols.name: traits
symbols.doc: `(word_fatal, repairable)` for a code; an unknown code is a lead with no repair.

symbols.name: RING1_CODES
symbols.doc: Codes the Ring-1 checks own; the triage checks' findings under these codes are the same problems seen twice and are left out of [`validate`].

symbols.name: ValidateError
symbols.doc: Why a package could not be validated at all (a finding is never an error).

symbols.name: Repaired
symbols.doc: The package with every repairable finding fixed, the findings it fixed and the ones it could not.

symbols.name: validate_with
symbols.signature: pub fn validate_with( docx: &[u8], rules: &[&str], original: Option<(&[u8], &str)>, layout: Option<crate::audit::LayoutPass<'_>>, ) -> Result<Vec<Finding>, ValidateError>
symbols.doc: [`validate`] with rule sets: `word` (the default), `edits`, and the [`crate::audit`] sets or codes (`a11y`, `style`, `structure`, `LITERAL_BULLET`, ...).

symbols.name: unknown_rule
symbols.doc: The usage message for a rule that is neither a set nor an audit code.

symbols.name: fails
symbols.signature: pub fn fails(findings: &[Finding], strict: bool) -> bool
symbols.doc: True when `findings` fail a run: any `word` or `edits` finding, any `error`, or (`strict`) any `warning`.

symbols.name: findings_text
symbols.doc: One line per finding, then a summary.

symbols.name: from
symbols.doc: The audit's finding in the shared shape: its part is the story's part for a paragraph id (`p3` → `word/document.xml`), else the location itself (a part name); it is never Word-fatal or repairable.

symbols.name: validate
symbols.doc: Findings sorted by part, location, code and message (the same order every run); an empty vector is a pass.

symbols.name: ring1
symbols.doc: The Ring-1 invariants alone, on an opened package: no admission, no triage checks.

symbols.name: check_style_names
symbols.doc: A style's `w:name` holds no comma: the schema's pattern is `[^,]*` (Word reads a comma there as the start of an alias list), while its `w:styleId` may hold one.

symbols.name: check_runs_inside_paragraphs
symbols.doc: A run outside any paragraph: Word loads the document empty.

symbols.name: BLOCKS
symbols.doc: Story and cell containers: a run reaching one before any paragraph is outside a paragraph, whatever wraps it on the way.

symbols.name: element_path
symbols.doc: `w:body[0]/w:p[3]/w:r[2]`: conventional prefix and local name with the index among same-named siblings, root excluded.

symbols.name: check_namespace_qname_contexts
symbols.doc: Every prefix an MC prefix list names (`mc:Choice/@Requires`, `mc:Ignorable`, …) is bound where it is named, in every XML part: Word rejects a header whose `mc:Choice Requires="wps"` names an unbound `wps`.

symbols.name: check_relationship_integrity
symbols.doc: Every `r:id` / `r:embed` / `r:link` in a part resolves in that part's `.rels`; no duplicate rIds; no dangling internal targets.

symbols.name: check_picture_bullets
symbols.doc: Every `w:lvlPicBulletId` names a `w:numPicBullet` of the same numbering part: Word refuses the whole package otherwise ("document loaded empty").

symbols.name: UNIQUE_REVISION_IDS
symbols.doc: Revision elements whose `w:id` must be unique within a part.

symbols.name: collect_ids
symbols.signature: fn collect_ids( dom: &Dom, root: NodeId, rev_ids: &mut HashSet<String>, docpr_ids: &mut HashSet<String>, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, part: &str, )

symbols.name: para_id_values
symbols.doc: `(attribute, value)` pairs of `w14:paraId` / `w14:textId` values at or above Word's `0x80000000` bound, in `xml`.

symbols.name: check_del_text_under_del
symbols.doc: `w:del` must carry `w:delText` (never `w:t`).

symbols.name: covered_by_deletion
symbols.doc: True when a `w:del` or `w:moveFrom` covers `node` in its own story (a text box's `w:txbxContent` is a separate story).

symbols.name: check_deleted_text_has_deletion
symbols.doc: `w:delText` / `w:delInstrText` must sit under a `w:del` (or `w:moveFrom`) in its OWN story.

symbols.name: SINGLE_VALUE_CONTROLS
symbols.doc: Content controls whose content is a single value: Word keeps no bookmark in them.

symbols.name: bookmarks_in_single_value_controls
symbols.signature: fn bookmarks_in_single_value_controls( dom: &Dom, root: NodeId, ) -> Vec<(NodeId, &'static str, String)>
symbols.doc: `(bookmark mark, kind, control)` for every bookmark start or end inside a single-value content control.

symbols.name: check_bookmarks_outside_single_value_controls
symbols.doc: No bookmark start or end in a plain-text, dropdown, combo box, date, picture or checkbox content control.

symbols.name: ancestor_has
symbols.signature: fn ancestor_has(dom: &Dom, node: NodeId, stop: NodeId, local: &str) -> bool

symbols.name: comment_finding
symbols.signature: fn comment_finding(out: &mut Vec<Finding>, code: &str, part: &str, message: String)
symbols.doc: A finding of the comment family: `code` on `part`, no path.

symbols.name: comment_id_counts
symbols.signature: fn comment_id_counts(dom: &Dom, root: NodeId, local: &str) -> HashMap<String, usize>
symbols.doc: How often each id occurs on `local` elements.

symbols.name: check_hex_id
symbols.signature: fn check_hex_id( label: &str, value: &str, word_para_bound: bool, part: &str, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, )

symbols.name: check_comments_extended
symbols.signature: fn check_comments_extended( pkg: &PartFs, last_para_ids: &HashSet<String>, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, ) -> Option<ExtendedGraph>

symbols.name: check_comments_ids
symbols.signature: fn check_comments_ids( pkg: &PartFs, last_para_ids: &HashSet<String>, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, ) -> Option<HashSet<String>>

symbols.name: check_comments_extensible
symbols.signature: fn check_comments_extensible( pkg: &PartFs, expected_durable_ids: Option<&HashSet<String>>, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, )

symbols.name: attribute_by_local
symbols.signature: fn attribute_by_local<'a>(dom: &'a Dom, element: NodeId, local: &str) -> Option<&'a str>

symbols.name: check_exact_key_set
symbols.signature: fn check_exact_key_set( label: &str, actual: &HashSet<String>, expected: &HashSet<String>, part: &str, out: &mut Vec<Finding>, )

symbols.name: is_namespace_qname_list
symbols.doc: An unqualified `Requires` is a prefix list only on `mc:Choice`; on any other element (a custom XML part) it is application data.

symbols.name: namespace_in_scope
symbols.signature: fn namespace_in_scope<'a>(dom: &'a Dom, element: NodeId, prefix: &str) -> Option<&'a str>

symbols.name: repair
symbols.doc: The package with every repairable finding fixed, in a fixed order: unbound MC prefixes bound on the part root, `w:t`/`w:delText` swapped, bookmarks dropped from single-value controls, dangling relationship attributes dropped, duplicate drawing and revision ids renumbered, paragraph ids brought into Word's range, cells...

symbols.name: edit_part
symbols.signature: fn edit_part(pkg: &mut PartFs, part: &str, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Dom, NodeId))
symbols.doc: Parse `part`, let `f` change it, write it back.

symbols.name: fix_deleted_text
symbols.doc: `w:t` and `w:instrText` under a deletion become `w:delText` and `w:delInstrText`; `w:delText` under a move source, and deleted text no deletion covers, become live text again.

symbols.name: drop_bookmarks_in_single_value_controls
symbols.doc: Every bookmark whose start or end sits in a single-value content control is dropped whole (both marks, wherever the other one is).

symbols.name: REQUIRES_RELATIONSHIP
symbols.doc: Elements whose `r:id` the schema requires: without the relationship the element itself has to go, not just the attribute.

symbols.name: drop_dangling_relationship_attributes
symbols.doc: Relationship attributes (`r:id`, `r:embed`, `r:link`, …) naming no relationship of the part are dropped, which is what stops Word's "unreadable content" repair.

symbols.name: renumber_duplicate_revision_ids
symbols.doc: A second use of a revision id is renumbered from the part's highest `w:id` upwards; a move range start takes its end along.

symbols.name: renumber_out_of_range_para_ids
symbols.doc: Every `w14:paraId` / `w14:textId` at or above `0x80000000` is masked into Word's range, and every reference to it (`paraIdParent`, the comment parts) follows.

symbols.name: end_cells_with_a_paragraph
symbols.doc: A table cell whose last child (its properties aside) is not a paragraph gets an empty one.

symbols.name: drop_orphan_comment_anchors
symbols.signature: fn drop_orphan_comment_anchors(dom: &mut Dom, root: NodeId, defined: &HashSet<String>)
symbols.doc: Comment range marks and references naming no comment definition are dropped; a run left holding only its properties goes with its reference.

symbols.name: all_paragraphs
symbols.doc: The body's paragraphs followed by every story's (`header1`, ...).

symbols.name: story_part
symbols.doc: The part a paragraph or change id lives in: the body's (`p3`, `r12`) is the main document, any other story's (`header1.p1`, `footnotes.r2`) `word/{story}.xml`.

symbols.name: audit_tracked
symbols.signature: pub fn audit_tracked( original: &[u8], edited: &[u8], author: &str, ) -> Result<Vec<Finding>, ValidateError>
symbols.doc: `validate.py --original --author` without an XSD: every visible-text difference between `original` and `edited` must sit in a revision by `author`.

symbols.name: as_edits
symbols.doc: [`audit_tracked`]'s findings belong to the `edits` set and fail a run.

symbols.name: WmlDocument
symbols.doc: A WordprocessingML document held as its package bytes plus the main document part parsed on demand.

symbols.name: from_bytes
symbols.doc: Opens `bytes` as a `.docx`, admits it under [`InputLimits::compare`](crate::admission::InputLimits::compare), and lazily parses the main document part on the first [`Self::main_document`] call.

symbols.name: bytes
symbols.doc: The bytes the document was opened from.

symbols.name: main_document_part_name
symbols.doc: The main document part name (`word/document.xml` unless OPC relationships name otherwise).

symbols.name: main_document
symbols.signature: pub fn main_document(&mut self) -> Result<NodeId, OpcError>
symbols.doc: Parses the main document part (once) and returns its document node.

symbols.name: main_document_root
symbols.signature: pub fn main_document_root(&mut self) -> Result<NodeId, OpcError>
symbols.doc: The root element (`<w:document>`) of the main document part.

symbols.name: dom
symbols.doc: The arena DOM (read-only).

symbols.name: dom_mut
symbols.doc: The arena DOM (mutable).

symbols.name: part_fs
symbols.doc: The opened OPC package (read-only), by which every other part and relationship is read.

symbols.name: part_fs_mut
symbols.doc: The opened OPC package (mutable).
